send.python:
import os
from sendhog import SendHog

client = SendHog(os.environ['SENDHOG_API_KEY'])

result = client.send({
    "from": "sender@example.com",
    "to": "recipient@example.net",
    "subject": "Hello from SendHog",
    "text": "Hello from your application."
})
print(result['id'])
send.curl:
# Native SendHog HTTP; the SDK translates the SendHog call above.
curl 'https://app.sendhog.com/v1/send' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENDHOG_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "from": "sender@example.com",
  "to": [
    "recipient@example.net"
  ],
  "subject": "Hello from SendHog",
  "text": "Hello from your application."
}'

import os
from sendhog import SendHog

client = SendHog(os.environ['SENDHOG_API_KEY'])

# SendHog extension; requires email.read scope.
page = client.messages.list(direction='received', limit=20)
if page['data']:
    message = client.messages.get(page['data'][0]['id'])
    print(message['subject'], message['text'])

import os
from sendhog.postmark import ServerClient

import asyncio

async def main():
    async with ServerClient(os.environ['SENDHOG_API_KEY']) as client:
        result = await client.outbound.send({
            "sender": "sender@example.com",
            "to": "recipient@example.net",
            "subject": "Hello from SendHog",
            "text_body": "Hello from your application."
        })
        print(result.message_id)

asyncio.run(main())
